title: Clark Painting vs. Precision Paint Experts
description: Comparing Clark Painting and Precision Paint Experts for kitchen cabinets? What to ask about cabinet prep, finish systems, and cure time before you decide.
h1: Clark Painting vs. Precision Paint Experts
heroIntro: Cabinet painting is closer to furniture finishing than wall painting. This guide covers the finish-system questions to ask any North Central Florida contractor.

keywords.primary: clark painting vs precision paint experts
questions: What kind of paint should be used on kitchen cabinets?
Is it better to refinish or replace kitchen cabinets?

body: Clark Painting is one of the painting and property-service companies North Central Florida homeowners may be comparing. If your project centers on kitchen or bathroom cabinets, the comparison should go deeper than color and price. Cabinet doors are opened, wiped, and bumped every day, and a finish that looks perfect at handoff can start to chip or feel tacky within months if the product or prep was wrong.
This guide lays out what to ask any contractor about cabinet work and what Precision Paint Experts specifies, so you have a clear benchmark.

Wall paint is not designed for cabinets. Ask every bidder which primer and topcoat they will use on doors, boxes, and drawer fronts, and get the product line in writing. For cabinets, doors, and railings we use waterborne urethane enamel from premium Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore lines. It is built for hard-use surfaces and is named on our estimate, along with the number of coats.

Two full coats is our baseline. On a dramatic change, such as dark stained oak going to white, a third coat is added. Our article on painting oak cabinets explains why grain and tannins need special attention.

sections.h2: Cabinet questions to bring to every estimate
body: Use this list during each walkthrough:
bullets: Which products, and how many coats, on doors and on cabinet boxes?
How will surfaces be cleaned and sanded before priming?
Are interiors of the boxes included or excluded?
How will the color be matched or confirmed before work starts?
What should I avoid doing while the finish cures?

body: For many kitchens, solid cabinet boxes in a layout you like are worth keeping, and a proper finish system can change the room without the cost and mess of a tear-out. For others, damaged boxes or a layout that no longer works make replacement the better call. Our guide on refinishing versus replacing cabinets walks through the trade-offs honestly. If you are dealing with a previous paint job that is already failing, see what to do about peeling cabinet paint.

A crew lead walks the kitchen, measures, and photographs current conditions. The written estimate lists every surface included and excluded, the prep steps, the products by name, and the schedule. We can match color from a chip, an existing cabinet door, or a leftover can, with full-size drawdowns you can see in your own lighting. Learn more on our cabinet painting and refinishing page.

A cabinet walkthrough can usually be booked within 48 hours, with the itemized quote typically in your inbox one business day later. Compare its product names, coat counts, and exclusions against any other cabinet bid you receive. If two quotes differ widely, the finish system and prep steps are almost always where the gap lives, so ask both contractors to explain their choices in plain terms.

faqs.q: What paint do you use on kitchen cabinets?
faqs.a: Waterborne urethane enamel from premium Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore lines, named on your estimate.

faqs.q: Can you match my cabinets to an existing door?
faqs.a: Yes. We can color-match from a cabinet door, a chip, or a leftover can, and show full-size drawdowns before work begins.

faqs.q: Is Precision Paint Experts related to Clark Painting?
faqs.a: No. We are a separate, locally owned company. This page is a guide for comparing cabinet painting estimates.
Only if they are listed. Our estimates state which surfaces are included and excluded so you know exactly what is covered.
